summary: Jon Postel's comment on RFC 467, endorsing its proposal to resynchronize the state of a Host-Host connection with one small change. He suggests naming the commands RAS and RAR, reset allocation sender and receiver, since only the allocation is reset, and includes a table of the procedure.

eli5.summary: Someone liked a plan for fixing stuck network conversations, suggested better names for two of the steps, and drew a chart of how it works.

subtitle: Postel suggests better names for connection recovery commands.

tldr.problem: RFC 467 proposed a procedure to recover when the Host-Host connection got out of synchronization and lost track of how much data each side could send.
tldr.mechanism: Jon Postel endorsed the proposal and renamed the two commands RAS (reset allocation sender) and RAR (reset allocation receiver) to clarify that only the sending allowances, not the entire connection, were being reset. He included a table showing the synchronization sequence.
tldr.outcome: The new names made the purpose of the recovery procedure clearer and were adopted in later protocol specifications.

today: RFC 489 is a historical comment on an early protocol proposal from 1973. These concepts evolved into modern connection management and flow control in TCP and other protocols.

sections.title: Connection Recovery
sections.content: This RFC is Jon Postel's brief comment on a proposal by Burchfiel and Tomlinson in RFC 467. The Host-Host protocol needs a way to recover when both communicating hosts lose synchronization about how much data each side is allowed to send. The allocation is a critical part of the flow control mechanism, and when it gets out of sync, the connection becomes stuck.
sections.eli5: Computers talking over the network need a way to fix the situation when they forget who said what and get confused.

sections.title: The RAS and RAR Commands
sections.content: Postel proposes renaming the recovery commands to RAS (reset allocation sender) and RAR (reset allocation receiver). These names are more precise than the original proposal, because they emphasize that only the allocation quantities are being reset, not the whole connection. The sender and receiver follow a sequence: the sender sets a wait state, waits for outstanding acknowledgments, sends RAS, and processes responses until receiving RAR. The receiver sends RAR, processes incoming messages, receives RAS, zeros its allocation, and returns to open state.
sections.eli5: Two new commands, RAS and RAR, let the sender and receiver fix how much data each one can send, step by step, until they agree again.

sections.title: Synchronization Procedure
sections.content: The procedure can be initiated by either the sender or receiver, and either for reasons of its own or after receiving a RAS or RAR command from the other side. The RFC provides a concise side-by-side table showing what each side does at each step. This recovery mechanism is critical to ensuring reliable connection management in the early Host-Host protocol.
sections.eli5: Either side of the conversation can start the fix, and there is a clear sequence of steps that brings them back into sync.

references.text: Burchfiel, J. and Tomlinson, R., "Proposed Host-Host Protocol", RFC 467, April 1973.
